title: 'The things dreams are made of' - Cherries fans in Prague for Europa League clash

PRAGUE was the destination for the Cherries fans on the second step of the club’s European tour, and the fans painted the town red and black ahead of their side’s game against Sparta Praha. Bournemouth were heading into the game off the back of three victories in their first three European games. It was a special occasion in San Sebastian as Marco Rose’s side got up and running in the competition, before big home wins against Sturm Graz and AC Milan at home. Jeff Mostyn (Image: Newsquest) Former Cherries chairman Jeff Mostyn, who played a crucial role in the club’s rise from the bottom of the Football League to the top, couldn’t make the game in the Basque country but said he would not have missed this one ‘for love nor money’. “It's surreal, absolutely surreal,” Mostyn told the Daily Echo. “To be in this incredible Old Town Square, the centre of Prague with all the magnificent buildings surrounded by Cherries supporters. “I mean, it's just the things that dreams are made of!” Mostyn was out with Cherries fans the night before the game, and said: “There was so much love in this Irish bar last night, I cannot tell you. “I was totally and utterly humbled by the kindness and the kind words that people afforded me and had to make sure that they knew that I was just one person that had played what he thought or I thought was a small part in this incredible club's history.” He added: “For me this trip is all about the supporters. “People have told me in the past that owners, chairman, managers, players all come and go. “The one constant than any football club are the supporters. “So for them I'm the happiest man alive that they've supported the club all their life. “Not one of them would ever have thought that one day that they could be stood in Old Town Square in Prague supporting their incredible Cherries.” Cherries fan Guy Naish had just arrived in Prague when he spoke to the Daily Echo, and he was feeling confident ahead of the game. “We've turned a bit of a corner, haven't we?” he said. “The fact that we're going into this this game with a bit of form, I think is very positive, the fact we haven't conceded for quite some time. “I think it's a record to be broken tonight if we can complete the first 45 minutes, score a goal and not concede. “So yeah, it's honestly amazing times to be a Bournemouth fan.” AFC Bournemouth Football Sport Bournemouth Share 0 Comments Get involved with the news Send your news &
